minutes.headline: Task force agreed to hold off buying the Unitil streetlights until closer to the LED grant; RFP work set for February
minutes.summary: The task force reviewed Unitil's streetlight purchase proposal and December bill, and the timing of the next Green Communities competitive grant. Members leaned toward delaying the purchase, pressing Unitil for equipment age data, and starting RFP work at a meeting in February. Some current grant projects likely cannot be finished by the February deadline, so the October round is the target.

what_happened.line: The task force reached consensus to hold off buying the Unitil streetlights while it seeks equipment age data from Unitil, to keep the town's ownership period short.
Members agreed to reconvene next month to begin developing the RFP and to review the documents already sent.
The task force reviewed Unitil's purchase proposal and the December bill, most of which is maintenance rather than electricity.
Some current grant projects, including the primary school hot water heater, will likely not be finished under the grant, so the October round is the target.
The next meeting is to be set in February, with Thursdays preferred, pending a member's schedule. No votes were taken apart from adjournment.

why_it_matters: The town keeps paying Unitil for streetlight maintenance and power until it owns the lights, so the timing of a purchase decides how long that bill continues and when a LED conversion, which could lower it, can begin.
Buying the lights would put maintenance and net metering credits on the town budget, mostly taxes, so a purchase vote would likely reach residents later.
